title: add interleaved-qkv concat + fused-reduction kernel with rotary preapply and kv-prefetch scheduler
author: Eleanor Briggs
description:
Motivation: reduce tail latency and peak memory pressure for high-concurrency, small-batch serving scenarios by (1) fusing QKV interleave + concat followed by a single reduction kernel to avoid extra device memory transposes, (2) applying rotary/rope positional transforms as an inline fused op (preapply) to remove an extra KV write/read, and (3) introducing a light-weight KV-prefetch policy in the continuous-batching scheduler to warm slab cache for hot prefixes. This PR implements a new CUDA kernel suite (attn_interleave_fused_reduction.cu/h), runtime hooks, and scheduler policy flags.

Changes included: checklist: - [x] new interleaved QKV concat + fused reduction kernel with half-float/INT8-friendly paths - [x] fused rotary/rope preapply (optional per-model flag) to avoid a separate rotary kernel pass - [x] KV-prefetch scheduler strategy that issues async prefetches for hot route prefixes when batch size < target but concurrency high - [x] unit tests for kernel correctness (QK normalization, softmax numerics, gradient parity in training-mode builds) - [x] integration tests in the runtime CPU/GPU CI matrix - [x] perf harness and microbenchmarks committed under benchmark-lab/attn-prefetch/ - [x] documented runtime config flags and migration notes in CHANGELOG and docs snippet - [x] rollout plan with canary percentage and automatic rollback on p95 latency regression > 10%

Design notes: We observed two key overheads in microbenchmarks for 1-4 token sequences at batch sizes 1-8 and high concurrency: (A) extra global memory transposes between Q,K,V layouts; (B) repeated rotary application that materializes KV and causes eviction pressure. The new interleaved kernel accepts packed QKV (interleaved along head dim) and computes attention reductions in-place producing output without an intermediate full shuffle. The fused rotary preapply accepts rotary parameters and applies them to Q/K lanes in the same kernel launch; this is gated by model metadata so models without rotary/rope skip the path. Kernel implements numerically-stable scaled softmax and supports autoregressive KV-caching via an optional stream that writes into the slab cache with write-combining hints.

Scheduler change: introduce scheduler flag continuous_batcher.prefetch_policy with options [off, heuristic, aggressive]. Heuristic mode issues prefetches when observed reuse heatmap for prefix route > 0.6 and concurrency > 16; aggressive warms if p50 latency > target SLO and memory headroom available. Prefetches are issued with a low-priority CUDA stream to avoid head-of-line contention. Backpressure: prefetch is canceled if runtime memory estimator signals > 85% reserved.

Benchmarks: microbench harness (bench/attn_small_seq.py) results on p4d-like instance: - baseline (main): p50=10.8ms, p95=34.2ms, tokens/sec=5.6k - this PR (heuristic prefetch, fused kernels): p50=7.1ms (-34%), p95=20.9ms (-39%), tokens/sec=7.8k (+39%) for 1-4 token sequences, batch sizes 1-4. For larger sequences (>256) and large batch sizes, difference is neutral (+/-2%) indicating no regression on standard throughput paths. Memory: peak device allocation decreased ~18% on average for small-batch workloads.

Compatibility and flags: The new kernels are feature-gated. Default rollout: feature disabled by default; enabled via runtime config attn_fusion.enabled=true and per-model catalog flag model_config.attn.fusion=auto. We provide two modes: fast-path (fused rotary preapply + fused reduction) and compatibility-path (concat interleave only). Models can be pinned to either. No change to public API.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for numerical parity against baseline single-head reference, long-run stability test (24h concurrency emulation), and a memory-leak smoke test. CI initially failed due to a missing device sync in the prefetch cancellation path; fixed and re-ran. Load-test canary at 5% traffic for three hours showed stable p95 improvements and no error spike.

Rollout plan: 1) merge to main behind feature flag, 2) enable on staging for dominated low-latency routes (messaging/chat), 3) 5% canary production for 3h, 4) 25% if metrics stable, 5) global if no regression after 24h. Automatic rollback rule: if p95 increases >10% or error-rate increases >0.1% relative.

Notes: This PR focuses on serving runtime; training kernels are untouched. Added comments in attn_interleave_fused_reduction.cu about vectorization choices and fallback heuristics for non-contiguous QKV layouts. Potential follow-ups: integrate per-head quantization-aware reduction, extend prefetch heatmap to persistent ML model predictions of prefix reuse, and explore fused dispatch for multi-query attention in transformer-decoder-lite variants.

review_thread: Marco Chen: Nice work on the kernel. A few nitpicks on register pressure and unrolling. Please add a fallback for non-native layout; see inline.
Eleanor Briggs: Added layout fallback path and comments explaining tradeoffs; kept fast-path register allocation after microbenching.
Priya Raman: Scheduler looks good but the 0.6 heatmap threshold should be configurable via runtime flag. Also add telemetry for canceled prefetches.
Eleanor Briggs: Exposed heatmap threshold as continuous_batcher.heatmap_threshold and added telemetry event prefetch.canceled + reason tags.
Samir Patel: CI failure reproduced locally; good catch on missing device synchronize. Approving after fix.
release_notes: Introduce interleaved QKV fused-reduction kernel and optional fused rotary preapply to improve small-batch latency and reduce memory pressure; add KV-prefetch scheduler policy to warm slab cache for hot prefixes. Feature gated; off by default. See docs/perf/attn_fusion.md for configuration and rollout guidance.
